An Overview for Living in Extraterrestrial Universe without DNA & RNA: Higgs Boson or God Particle as a Common Origin for Universal Life and Living Essence Existence
works.abstract: Obviously, the initial biopolymer for any type of universal life on another planet must satisfy other construction of life. Therefore, synthetic enzymes hinted related to cosmic life without DNA or RNA might be produced in another part of the universe. Enzymes can be made from quasi genetic material that does not exist on Earth. So, this discussion is a fundamental theory for the possibility of life that could evolve without DNA or RNA (whom these two self-replicating units for life on Earth). Our universe is surprising in many aspects, allowing for everything we see to exist. Therefore our universe might be the exception that is balanced in this way, and it is only in this balance can there be life. Interestingly, 3 quarks could still exist without the Higgs field, but the electron would remain massless, which means there would no longer be atoms of any kind, no biomolecules, DNA, RNA, and no life.

works.title: High‐Resolution Multi‐Isotope Imaging Mass Spectrometry (MIMS) Imaging Applications in Stem Cell Biology
works.abstract: Multi-isotope imaging mass spectrometry (MIMS) allows the measurement of turnover of molecules within intracellular compartments with a spatial resolution down to 30 nm. We use molecules enriched in stable isotopes administered to animals by diet or injection, or to cells through the culture medium. The stable isotopes used are, in general, 15 N, 13 C, 18 O, and 2 H. For stem cell studies, we essentially use 15 N-thymidine, 13 C-thymidine, and 81 Br from BrdU. This protocol describes the practical use of MIMS with specific reference to applications in stem cell research. This includes choice and administration of stable isotope label(s), sample preparation, best practice for high-resolution imaging, secondary ion mass spectrometry using the Cameca NanoSIMS 50L, and methods for robust statistical analysis of label incorporation in regions of interest (ROI). © 2021 The Authors. Current Protocols published by Wiley Periodicals LLC. Basic Protocol 1: Stable isotope labeling of DNA in cultured cells Basic Protocol 2: Stable isotope labeling of DNA in animals Basic Protocol 3: Preparation of Si chips, the general sample support for NanoSIMS analysis Basic Protocol 4: Stable isotope analysis of DNA replication in single nuclei in a population of cells with NanoSIMS Basic Protocol 5: Data reduction and processing.

works.title: Xenobiology: An expanded semantical review
works.abstract: The definition of “xenobiology” has gradually shifted from the study of the foreign, estranged life forms potentially existing in outer space to the study where the natural and synthetic life are involved. The natural concept of xenobiology governs the unseen, hypothetical life on the outer space, and the hidden life with completely different biochemistry on Earth. The life on the outer space might possess different way to harvest energy from the one on Earth. The hidden life on Earth, or the “Shadow Biosphere” might rose from completely different way of creation and evolution on Earth, which lead to its complete difference from the known biosphere. The newest concept of xenobiology involves synthetic life, built with unnatural base pair of the nucleic acid, with analogous or xeno nucleic acid (XNA), has a synthetic genome which capable of self-replicating or enables the synthetic cell to self-replicate, or even possesses a synthetic physiological pathway. By understanding the broad spectrum of xenobiology, in both natural and synthetic concepts, we can expand our view on how life might develop into a completely estranged system, which is different from anthropocentric view of life available around us on Earth. From these perspectives, we might understand how life evolved by evolving it synthetically.

works.title: Thermodynamics of Prebiotic Phosphorylation
works.abstract: The formation of organophosphate molecules by prebiotic processes relies on nonenzymatic synthesis. Given the centrality of phosphorylated biomolecules in metabolic, structural, and replicative processes, it is highly likely that such nonenzymatic synthesis had to occur early in Earth's history. This Review collects and uses thermodynamic data to constrain processes that may have produced organophosphates and evaluates both the plausibility of reactants and the likelihood that environments conducive to phosphorylation were present. The energy required to phosphorylate organics is ∼15 kJ/mol, requiring either very low water activities or reactive inorganic phosphorus compounds. Thermodynamics permits evaluating phosphorylation environments for both plausibility and novelty and shows that several routes would have been available to form these potentially key reagents. Building from phosphate monoesters to diesters may have enabled the synthesis of nucleic acids, perhaps opening a way into the RNA world.

works.title: The Origin of the Ionized Linker: Geochemical Predestination for Phosphate?
Problem Simplification
The Purpose of Data Analysis Is to Enable Data Reanalysis
What Lies Within: Superscripting References to Reveal Research Trends
works.abstract: Interpreting scholarly contributions solely on the basis of the number, and not nature, of citations is inherently flawed because contradictory as well as confirmatory findings feed into the same metric, capturing popularity at the expense of precision. I propose a citation and indexing procedure that would conveniently integrate information about research trends while imposing minimal burden on the producers and consumers of research. Under the proposed system, citations appearing in the reference list of research reports would be superscripted with letters corresponding to one of the following six categories: references to findings that are Consistent with the current findings, are Replicated by the current findings, are Inconsistent with the current findings, Failed to be replicated by the current findings, were used to build Theory, or were used to cite Methodologies. I explain how the resulting CRIF-TM data could be summarized and perpetually updated by an online indexing service. I provide an example to demonstrate how these superscripts could be conveniently and unobtrusively presented in the reference list of forthcoming articles. Finally, I examine the anticipated benefits, limitations, and implementation challenges of the proposed citation and indexing procedure.

works.title: Nucleotide insertion initiated by van der Waals interaction during polymerase beta DNA replication
Structural and Functional Consequences of Phosphate–Arsenate Substitutions in Selected Nucleotides: DNA, RNA, and ATP
works.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
works.abstract: A recent finding of a bacterial strain (GFAJ-1) that can rely on arsenic instead of phosphorus raised the questions of if and how arsenate can replace phosphate in biomolecules that are essential to sustain cell life. Apart from questions related to chemical stability, there are those of the structural and functional consequences of phosphate-arsenate substitutions in vital nucleotides in GFAJ1-like cells. In this study we selected three types of molecules (ATP/ADP as energy source and replication regulation; DNA-protein complexes for DNA replication and transcription initiation; and a tRNA-protein complex and ribosome for protein synthesis) to computationally probe if arsenate nucleotides can retain the structural and functional features of phosphate nucleotides. Hydrolysis of adenosine triarsenate provides 2-3 kcal/mol less energy than ATP hydrolysis. Arsenate DNA/RNA interacts with proteins slightly less strongly than phosphate DNA/RNA, mainly due to the weaker electrostatic interactions of arsenate. We observed that the weaker arsenate RNA-protein interactions may hamper rRNA assembly into a functional ribosome. We further compared the experimental EXAFS spectra of the arsenic bacteria with theoretical EXAFS spectra for arsenate DNA and rRNA. Our results demonstrate that while it is possible that dried GFAJ-1 cells contain linear arsenate DNA, the arsenate 70S ribosome does not contribute to the main arsenate depository in the GFAJ-1 cell. Our study indicates that evolution has optimized the inter-relationship between proteins and DNA/RNA, which requires overall changes at the molecular and systems biology levels when replacing phosphate by arsenate.

works.title: Pharmacophore-Guided Drug Repurposing Identifies Galicaftor as a Potential Ligand for Pseudouridine Synthase 7
works.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pseudouridine synthase 7 (PUS7) supports tumor growth in glioblastoma, neuroblastoma, and other malignancies through catalysis-dependent mechanisms. Although PUS7 is a potential pharmacological target for cancer therapy, only a few small-molecule inhibitors have been reported, and their binding modes remain experimentally unresolved. This study aimed to identify approved and investigational drugs with the potential to bind to the PUS7 catalytic site. Methods: Unresolved regions of the crystal structure of human PUS7 (PDB ID: 5KKP) were reconstructed using homology modeling. Conformational variability of the apo enzyme was investigated using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free-energy surface analysis, and robust Perron cluster analysis. A dynamic target-based pharmacophore was generated and used to screen the DrugBank library. The stability of the resulting pharmacophore-matched compounds as PUS7 binders was assessed using MD simulations and MM-PBSA analysis. Results: Four metastable states of PUS7 were identified and used to characterize a consistently identified pocket within the catalytic domain. This pocket was then used to construct an ensemble pharmacophore comprising five features, with occupancies ranging from 11% to 74%. Nine compounds were selected through pharmacophore screening. Galicaftor and canfosfamide exhibited favorable MM-PBSA binding free energy estimates; however, only galicaftor maintained consistent binding poses within the PUS7 catalytic cavity across independent MD replicates. Conclusions: Galicaftor is a potential binder of the PUS7 catalytic cavity. This compound is a candidate for drug repurposing and warrants experimental evaluation to determine its interactions with PUS7.

works.title: Noncanonical P gene mRNA editing in Cedar virus generates a U protein that is required for efficient virion production
works.abstract: Highly pathogenic Hendra and Nipah viruses encode accessory P gene products (C, V and W) that antagonize innate immunity and contribute to pathogenicity. Cedar virus (CedV), an apathogenic bat-borne henipavirus, is presumed to lack P gene mRNA editing and therefore is unable to express V and W proteins. Here, we identify CedV peptides originating from a frameshifted P gene open reading frame and demonstrate a previously unrecognized, noncanonical editing site at a homopolymeric adenine tract that introduces single-nucleotide A or G insertion. This mRNA editing produces a protein that we refer to as U protein, whose C-terminal domain shares sequence and predicted structural features with those of the henipavirus V protein. Recombinant CedV mutants defective in mRNA editing were only recoverable by trans-complementation and showed markedly reduced release of infectious virus in cell culture and attenuated replication in mice lacking type I interferon receptor. Our data revise the CedV gene expression models and reveal a noncanonical editing mechanism that supports the production of a U protein critical for efficient infectious virus release. These results expand the fundamental concepts of paramyxovirus gene expression and reveal an unexpected requirement for P-gene editing in efficient infectious-virus production, with implications for the evaluation of potentially high-consequence paramyxoviruses.

works.title: Replicon-based antiviral screening identifies Simeprevir and Mosnodenvir as inhibitors of Kyasanur Forest Disease virus
From decoction assembly to precision-oriented delivery: Antiviral roles of supramolecular complexes in traditional chinese medicine and food–medicine homology systems
works.abstract: Existing antiviral therapies are constrained by viral mutation, resistance, and adverse effects. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and food–medicine homology (FMH) resources provide alternative therapeutic avenues, yet modern pharmacological studies frequently attribute their efficacy to isolated monomeric compounds. This reductionist perspective neglects the supramolecular assemblies formed by polyphenols, polysaccharides, proteins, and other constituents via non-covalent interactions during decoction, processing, and gastrointestinal digestion. Because such assemblies alter apparent solubility, surface charge and interfacial behaviour, they may change the chemical form in which a constituent actually reaches the mucosa, and therefore the activity attributable to a given marker compound. This review examines antiviral TCM from a supramolecular perspective. We detail the formation of these assemblies during traditional preparation and digestion, and delineate their mechanisms across the viral life cycle, including entry blockade, replication inhibition, and gut–lung mucosal defense. Furthermore, the functional properties of TCM-derived natural nanoparticles and carrier-free delivery systems are evaluated. Classical compatibility principles and processing detoxification are reconceptualized as testable structure–function relationships. Current methodological limitations in structural characterization, safety evaluation, and multi-omics integration are critically discussed. Treating the assembled state as a defined experimental variable, rather than as an uncontrolled feature of the extract, is a prerequisite for moving from empirical formulation to structure–function-guided antiviral pharmacology.

works.title: Exploring conjugation between Streptomyces as a tool to mobilize biosynthetic gene clusters
works.abstract: Streptomyces bacteria harbor conjugative plasmids and integrative conjugative elements that employ a unique mode of DNA transfer. It minimally requires a single FtsK-like motor protein, TraB, and a cis -acting sequence recognized by TraB, clt. Notably, clt -like sequences (clc) are also scattered over Streptomyces chromosomes, driving the co-transfer of their macrofragments along with the plasmid. This could be used to facilitate the exchange of genetic material between different streptomycete strains and even species, thus creating new opportunities for natural product discovery. Here we explored several possible avenues of use of conjugation in the context of the popular chassis strain Streptomyces albidoflavus J1074, such as plasmid and chromosomal marker mobilization, and ability to transfer across species. First, among several clc types being screened in silico, the one for TraB encoded by plasmid pIJ101 was the most abundant. Second, TraB-mediated transfer of replicative (pIJ101-based) plasmid occurred at a frequency of 10% of recipient spore titer. The efficiency of inheritance of the chromosomal marker, distant to the conjugative plasmid location within the genome, was about four orders of magnitude lower. The developed methods might be useful to produce novel J1074 genotypes. Finally, we show that the removal of native plasmid-encoded clt site and repressor gene korA led to further drop (down to 10 − 6) in conjugation efficiency, albeit did not abrogate it completely. Hence, the prospects of chromosomal clc sites for gene transfer across species deserve more attention. We discuss the challenges associated with this genetic system and possible avenues for improvement, in the context of ongoing chassis-centered natural product discovery endeavors.

works.title: Design and proof of concept of a CRISPR/Cas13a-catalytic hairpin assembly framework for circulating microRNA detection in sepsis
works.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, largely because early diagnosis is slow. Current biomarkers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin lack specificity and need up to 24 h to peak, delaying diagnosis in a condition where each hour increases mortality risk. Circulating microRNAs are promising early biomarkers, reflecting rapid molecular changes in the host response to infection. We propose a diagnostic framework combining CRISPR/Cas13a molecular recognition with a Catalytic Hairpin Assembly amplification circuit. Cas13a is programmed to recognize a short microRNA; on activation it cleaves a synthetic substrate collaterally, releasing an initiator that triggers an enzyme-free amplification cascade. In a proof-of-concept experiment a complete redesigned hairpin set (H0, H1 and H2) raised the share of the hairpin pool migrating as the H1-H2 duplex from approximately 34% to approximately 90% relative to a published set used in the same architecture, measured as band intensity in parallel lanes of a single gel. This is reported as a preliminary observation: the comparison rests on technical replicates of one reaction and lacks the no-target control that would establish target-dependent operation of the complete cascade. The system is designed for integration into a portable microneedle-microfluidic biosensor that would permit minimally invasive, serial sampling with an end-to-end assay time of approximately 4 h per measurement; that device has not been built and is described here as a specification. The two microRNAs were chosen by exhaustive screening of a public whole-blood cohort. They separate septic patients from healthy volunteers well (ROC-AUC 0.95) but separate them from patients with non-infectious inflammation poorly (ROC-AUC 0.64), and no panel of up to 263 curated microRNAs improved on that second figure, which is the comparison that matters clinically. That evidence comes from whole blood, a cell-associated compartment, whereas the proposed device would sample interstitial fluid, which is cell-free; performance in the intended sample therefore remains an open question. This article presents a hypothesis and a design, together with the computational and bench evidence that bears on them. No sensitivity, specificity or clinical performance is claimed, and the experiments that would test the proposal are set out explicitly.

works.title: AlphaFold-Multimer reveals diverse cyclin-CDK substrate docking interactions
works.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) control eukaryotic cell-cycle progression by phosphorylating specific substrates with substrate recognition often involving cyclin-specific docking interactions. However, in minimal cell cycle control systems driven by a single cyclin-CDK complex, how docking interactions contribute to the differential timing of substrate phosphorylation remains unclear. Here, we used AlphaFold-Multimer to systematically predict interactions between the fission yeast mitotic cyclin-CDK fusion Cdc13-L-Cdc2 and its known in vivo CDK substrates. We found that many substrates are predicted to interact with the cyclin hydrophobic patch, and have identified a previously uncharacterised docking motif, [FVIPWGLAM](x)xER[LMV] (ERL motif), with features consistent with an atypical RxL motif. We show that ERL motifs can functionally substitute for canonical RxL motifs to promote phosphorylation of a model CDK substrate by Cdc13-Cdc2, while the S-phase cyclin-CDK Cig2-Cdc2 was found to preferentially phosphorylate substrates containing canonical RxL motifs. Interestingly, Cdc13-L-Cdc2 was not predicted to bind DNA replication substrates preferentially over mitotic substrates, suggesting that other mechanisms underlie the temporal ordering of CDK substrate phosphorylation. These results reveal that cyclin-CDK-substrate interactions are more diverse than previously thought.

works.title: Authentic structure of the CCHFV RNA–nucleoprotein complex at near-atomic resolution
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) poses a major public health threat without approved vaccines or antivirals. Its ribonucleoprotein (RNP) is essential for replication, but its native architecture and RNA packaging remain elusive. Here, we combine AI-based structural prediction with cryo-electron microscopy to resolve the native structure of the CCHFV RNP purified from CCHFV-infected cells. We report a 3.87 Å structure of a single-turn RNP, and local refinement yielded a 3.55 Å structure of two adjacent NP protomers with continuous RNA. This represents the highest-resolution authentic RNP structure reported among segmented negative-strand RNA viruses (sNSVs), and provides the structural basis for CCHFV RNP assembly. Together with mutational analyses, these findings define the molecular basis of RNA encapsidation and NP oligomerization in the native CCHFV RNP. Our findings provide a hybrid structural framework integrating AI and experimental approaches for understanding genome organization in sNSVs and offer a foundation for future antiviral development.

works.title: RhoH dysregulations in human diseases: a systematic review
works.venue: Egyptian Journal of Medical Human Genetics
works.abstract: RhoH is an atypical Rho GTPase that primarily regulates immunological functions in T-cells. Dysregulation of RhoH has been implicated in various diseases, particularly hematological cancers such as lymphoma and leukemia. However, recent studies have also identified aberrant RhoH expression in non-hematological conditions, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), chronic psoriasis, and epithelial cancer cell lines, despite RhoH being predominantly expressed in hematopoietic cells. Despite these findings, there has been limited systematic review of RhoH dysregulation across different human diseases. To address this gap, this systematic literature review (SLR) investigates the characteristics of RhoH dysregulation in both cancerous and non-cancerous human diseases, regardless of their hematological nature. Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines, we conducted a thorough search of three major scientific databases: PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, to identify relevant articles for analysis. The review focuses on two key themes: (1) the types of human diseases associated with RhoH dysregulation and (2) the specific characteristics of RhoH dysregulation. This comprehensive review enhances our understanding of the diverse diseases linked to RhoH dysregulation, providing a foundation for future research into its underlying mechanisms in signalling and disease pathogenesis.

works.title: Parasite-induced ER-PVM contacts promote CERT-dependent ceramide delivery to the apicomplexan vacuole
works.abstract: Apicomplexan parasites rely on host lipids for replication, yet how host transport machinery is coupled to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) remains unresolved. Here, we uncover a host-parasite membrane contact site mechanism driving ceramide delivery to the vacuole. Host ceramide transfer protein (CERT) targets the PVM via its PH domain, cooperating with host VAP-B to promote sphingolipid accumulation and support Toxoplasma and Plasmodium development. By combining VAP-B proximity labeling with FFAT motif predictions, we identified TgVPS13 as a parasite-encoded FFAT effector that physically engages host VAP-B at the host-parasite interface. Conditional depletion of TgVPS13 markedly reduces vacuolar sphingolipid enrichment, partially impairs host CERT recruitment at the PVM, disrupts intravacuolar parasite organization, and severely restricts replication. Together, these findings establish a model in which TgVPS13-VAP-B tethering creates ER-PVM proximity, organizing a functional contact site that optimizes CERT-mediated ceramide transfer for efficient host lipid acquisition.

works.title: An AI-designed, recombinantly produced FtsZ-directed peptide with in vitro activity against pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates
works.venue: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology

works.title: Proteome-wide reanalysis identifies coverage and error-rate limits on acquired lysines in cancer
works.abstract: Missense mutation in cancer creates acquired lysines, residues present in tumor cells and absent from normal cells in the same patient. The class holds 295,411 sites across 20,365 genes and falls on driver hotspots more often than other substitutions (odds ratio 1.68). Yet re-searching 42 proteomic experiments with a mutation-aware database recovers the mutant peptide in 0.63% of 8,470 site-in-cell-line observations, because a new lysine is a new cleavage site and the peptide it creates runs 6 residues against 13 for the wild type. Reported error rates do not hold either. Burden-matched entrapment puts the realized false-discovery proportion at 4.70% before score filtering, against 1% reported. Measured by competitive activity-based protein profiling across four cell lines, ligandability reproduces at the site level, no compound descriptor tested predicts it, and structure predicts it poorly at AUC 0.617. Acquired lysines are structurally ordinary, so the barrier is detection rather than chemistry.

works.title: Effects of temporal and parietal cortex non-invasive brain stimulation on memory in healthy older adults, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis
works.abstract: Memory decline is a common cognitive complaint among healthy older adults, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) has been investigated as a promising approach for enhancing memory. While most studies target the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, interest is growing in stimulating temporal and parietal areas due to their involvement in episodic and associative memory. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of temporo-parietal NIBS on memory in healthy older adults and patients with MCI and AD. Nineteen studies were included in the systematic review, of which 12 provided data for random-effects meta-analysis. Effects were expressed as Hedges' g, comparing active and sham stimulation. Overall, NIBS significantly improved memory performance (g = 0.67, 95% CI 0.27, 1.07). Analyses stratified by stimulation modality showed a significant effect for transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) (g = 0.81, 95% CI 0.08, 1.53), whereas repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) did not reach statistical significance (g = 0.60, 95% CI -0.0003, 1.19). The difference between modalities was not significant (p = 0.54). Additional analyses showed significant improvements in episodic memory across healthy older adults and patients with MCI and AD (g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.19, 1.01) and in patients with MCI and AD alone (g = 0.61, 95% CI 0.17, 1.06). rTMS did not significantly improve episodic memory in MCI and AD (g = 0.62, 95% CI -0.08, 1.31). These findings suggest potential memory benefits, but substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty of evidence warrant cautious interpretation.

works.title: Systematic Review of Population-Based Studies of Prevalence and Incidence of Aging-Associated Neurodegenerative Diseases in Russia
works.abstract: AIM: To systematically review population-based studies reporting the prevalence or incidence of dementia, cognitive dysfunction, and Parkinson's disease among adults aged 50 years and older in Russia. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and eLibrary from inception to January 2025, supplemented by grey-literature searches and citation checking. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting population-based prevalence or incidence estimates were eligible. Convenience samples from healthcare institutions and institutionalised populations without a population denominator were excluded, whereas population-based administrative records were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB-PrevMH tool. For studies using MMSE or Mini-Cog, projected dementia prevalence was calculated by adjusting screen-positive proportions for test sensitivity and specificity. Prevalence estimates were synthesised by inverse-variance meta-analysis on the logit scale, stratified by age group and ascertainment method. Random-effects estimates were considered primary; incidence estimates were not pooled. RESULTS: Twenty papers describing 17 distinct study populations met the inclusion criteria: 11 papers reported cognitive outcomes and 9 reported Parkinson's disease. Direct expert-diagnosis estimates of dementia prevalence were available from two older studies and ranged from 6.7% to 10.5% in adults older than 60 years. Registered prevalence based on administrative data was substantially lower, at approximately 0.5-0.6%. Screen-positive proportions based on MMSE or Mini-Cog ranged from 3.1% to 81.5%. After adjustment for test sensitivity and specificity, projected dementia prevalence reached 81.6% in a single Mini-Cog stratum aged 75-84 years; the random-effects pooled estimate for the nominal 75-84-year group was 54.1% (95% CI 18-87). Two screening strata were incompatible with the assumed test-accuracy parameters. Administrative estimates of Parkinson's disease prevalence ranged from 0.017% to 0.29%; the only neurologist-assessed population study reported 0.31%. CONCLUSION: Estimates varied markedly according to age, study design, and ascertainment method. Administrative data probably underestimate disease prevalence, whereas estimates derived from single cognitive screening tests are sensitive to assumptions about diagnostic accuracy. Available studies are regionally restricted and methodologically heterogeneous and do not provide reliable national prevalence or incidence estimates. Population-based longitudinal studies using validated diagnostic methods are needed to support health policy in Russia.

works.title: Effects of probiotics/synbiotic interventions on cognitive dysfunction in Alzheimer's or MCI: A systematic review and meta‑analysis of randomized controlled trials
Posttraumatic stress disorder and risk of all-cause dementia: A systematic review and meta-regression analysis of between-study heterogeneity
authors: Beatriz Gonçalves da Silva Miroski Gerente
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) has been associated with later-life dementia, but longitudinal evidence remains heterogeneous. We evaluated the association between PTSD and incident all-cause dementia and explored sources of between-study variability. METHODS: This systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251184132). We searched Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, PsycINFO and PTSDpubs for longitudinal cohort studies comparing incident dementia in individuals with and without PTSD. Hazard ratios (HRs) and odds ratios (ORs) were pooled separately. Subgroup analyses, leave-one-out analyses, meta-regression and publication-bias assessment were performed. FINDINGS: Thirteen longitudinal studies were included; 10 contributed to the HR meta-analysis, with a reported source-cohort population of 1,825,386. PTSD was associated with incident dementia in HR-based analyses (pooled HR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.39-2.20; I2 = 83.7%) and OR-based analyses (pooled OR, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.68-3.67; I2 = 84.2%). Leave-one-out analyses supported robustness. Weighted mean age explained 70.76% of between-study heterogeneity and remained significant in the multivariable model, together with follow-up duration. The full model explained 86.76% of residual heterogeneity. INTERPRETATION: PTSD was associated with incident all-cause dementia despite substantial heterogeneity. Baseline age and follow-up duration may partly explain between-study variability. These observational findings establish an association, not that PTSD causes dementia.

works.title: Effectiveness of Verbal Fluency Tests for Detecting Cognitive Decline in Adults with Alzheimer’s Dementia and Frontotemporal Dementia: A Three-Level Meta-Analysis
works.abstract: As our population ages, the prevalence of dementia, including Alzheimer's dementia (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), is increasing. Early dementia diagnoses facilitate access to interventions when they are most effective for prolonging and improving life. Verbal fluency tests (e.g., FAS and Animal Fluency) can aid in the diagnosis of AD and FTD through detecting declines in executive functioning and language. These tests may be particularly useful for diagnosing the behavioural variant of FTD (bvFTD), which is associated with declines in executive functioning. A systematic search of Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, MEDLINE, CINHAL, and AgeLine identified 127 peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to July 2024, which compared FAS and Animal Fluency Test performances of people with AD or FTD to cognitively-healthy controls. Hedges' g effect sizes determined the effectiveness of three common score types (Total, Intrusion, Perseveration) for AD/FTD combined, AD and combined FTD subtypes, and AD and FTD subtypes (e.g., bvFTD). FAS and Animal Fluency Total Scores were the most reported and effective for detecting cognitive decline in these dementias combined (g = -1.31 and g = -1.95, respectively), but similar effects were seen for AD and bvFTD. The pattern of effects was not influenced by patient characteristics and remained consistent when only low risk-of-bias studies were analysed. However, significant publication bias may have inflated the effects for AD. Overall, the FAS and Animal Fluency Total Scores can effectively detect cognitive decline in both AD and FTD, although they cannot be recommended for differentiating between AD and bvFTD.

works.title: From prospective memory to episodic future thinking in Alzheimer's disease and semantic dementia: A first comparative study
works.venue: Journal of Alzheimer s Disease Reports
works.abstract: Background Future-oriented cognition relies on prospective memory (PM), the ability to carry out intended actions, and episodic future thinking (EFT), the mental simulation of personal future events. How their breakdown relates to specific memory system failures in neurodegenerative diseases remains poorly understood. Objective To compare PM and EFT profiles, and their relationship as a function of temporal distance, in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) and semantic dementia (SD). Methods Ten patients with AD, ten with SD and 14 healthy controls completed an immersive virtual reality task assessing episodic memory and four PM conditions (time-based, semantically linked, non-linked and enacted event-based), and the Temporally Extended TEMPau task, assessing past and future episodic thinking at three temporal distances (one week, one year, five years). Results AD patients showed a generalized PM deficit and reduced EFT for near and intermediate timeframes, whereas distant EFT was relatively preserved. SD patients showed preserved time-based PM, a disproportionate failure for semantically linked event-based PM, milder impairment in non-linked conditions, and impaired EFT for intermediate and distant periods, with preserved near-future thinking. Although factual recall was preserved in SD, contextual binding and recognition were impaired. Neither group differed from controls on enacted PM. In the pooled sample, PM correlated with near-future EFT only, an association not replicated within groups. Conclusions Episodic and semantic memory appear to differentially support PM and EFT depending on temporal distance, with implications for the differential diagnosis and cognitive modeling of future-oriented processes in dementia.

works.title: Genome-Wide Genotype Resource and Exploratory Association Analysis of Alzheimer’s Disease in a Kazakh Population: A Case–Control Study
works.abstract: Background/Objectives: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) has a substantial genetic component, yet Central Asian populations remain markedly underrepresented in genomic studies of the disease. Methods: to address this gap, we generated array-based genotype data using an immune-focused genotyping platform from a Kazakh AD case–control cohort and performed an exploratory association analysis. Following quality control, 180 individuals of Kazakh ancestry, including 92 individuals with AD and 88 cognitively normal controls, were analyzed. Population structure was assessed using principal component analysis, and association testing was performed using covariate-adjusted logistic regression under an additive model (primary analysis), with case–control tests under several genetic models as secondary analyses. Results: no variant reached study-wide significance; however, several exploratory association signals (p < 1 × 10−4) were identified, including variants on chromosome 9p24 and in ADARB2, MAST4, and ADAM23, which remained nominally associated after adjustment for sex, age, and principal components. In addition, APOE ε4 carrier status was evaluated in cases and controls. The proportion of APOE ε4 carriers was numerically higher among individuals with AD than among controls (40.7% vs. 26.6%), although the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.074). These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require replication in larger independent cohorts. Conclusions: this study provides one of the first immune-focused array-based genotype datasets for AD in a Central Asian population. The publicly available genotype data and association results provide a foundation for future replication, meta-analysis, and comparative population-genetic studies of AD across diverse ancestry groups.

works.title: Reduced weighted permutation entropy in visual-temporal cortex and altered resting-state brain dynamics in Alzheimer’s disease
works.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed neural dynamics. Resting-state fMRI combined with signal-complexity measures may provide new insights into alterations in spontaneous brain activity. This study investigated whether weighted permutation entropy (WPE), an amplitude-sensitive measure of temporal complexity, could identify regional abnormalities in AD and characterize their temporal and network-level features. Methods: Twenty patients with AD and twenty-four healthy controls underwent resting-state fMRI. Regional WPE was calculated using the Brainnetome atlas. Group comparisons included age, sex, years of education, and mean framewise displacement as covariates. Brainnetome findings were evaluated at an exploratory uncorrected threshold of p < 0.001 and checked against Bonferroni correction across 246 regions. Selected regions were used for secondary seed-based functional connectivity analysis. Four complexity-drop cascade intervals were compared without multiplicity correction. Sensitivity analyses examined window length, AAL parcellation, and cascade recruitment thresholds of 8, 10, and 12 regions; Fourier-surrogate analyses provided an additional model-based assessment. Results: At the exploratory Brainnetome threshold, AD was associated with lower WPE in two right inferior temporal subregions and one left fusiform subregion; these findings did not survive Bonferroni correction across 246 regions. The AAL analysis showed a similar regional pattern under FDR correction (q < 0.05). Secondary seed-based analyses identified increased connectivity with visual, parietal, and sensorimotor regions. Longer Peak-to-End and Start-to-End cascade intervals were observed in AD at nominal p < 0.05, without correction across the four interval tests. The overall pattern of subsequent cascade analyses was retained at the 8- and 12-region thresholds. Conclusion: This small-sample study suggests that AD is associated with regional WPE differences, altered connectivity, and possible prolongation of complexity-drop cascades. The exploratory Brainnetome and temporal findings, together with within-sample AAL convergence, motivate independent replication with prespecified multiplicity control. These measures do not yet establish a clinical biomarker or a specific physiological mechanism.

works.title: Cognitive and brain reserve in bilingual speakers with clinical AD variants
works.venue: Alzheimer s & Dementia Diagnosis Assessment & Disease Monitoring
works.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bilingualism may confer resilience through enhanced neural integrity. However, evidence for its neuroprotective effect is mixed, and studies across Alzheimer's disease (AD) variants are limited. This study examined gray matter volume (GMV) differences between bilinguals and monolinguals with amnestic AD and logopenic variant primary progressive aphasia (lvPPA). METHODS: In 125 amnestic AD and 78 lvPPA participants with neuropsychological assessments and structural magnetic resonance imaging, we analyzed GMV differences between monolinguals and bilinguals within each variant, adjusting for demographic covariates. RESULTS: In amnestic AD, bilinguals showed lower GMV than monolinguals in several regions, including bilateral fusiform and right occipital regions, after correction for multiple comparisons. In lvPPA, regional differences did not survive correction for multiple comparisons, although at the nominal threshold, bilinguals showed lower GMV in temporal and occipital regions and greater GMV in inferior parietal regions. Cognitive performance was comparable between monolinguals and bilinguals within each group. DISCUSSION: Comparable cognitive performance despite lower GMV is consistent with a potential role of bilingualism in cognitive reserve. The observed regional patterns in lvPPA are exploratory and require replication in a larger sample.

works.title: Blood transcriptomic signatures of vascular risk in Alzheimer's disease
works.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lifestyle and environmental factors contributing to cardiovascular risk are components of the exposome, yet molecular signatures associated with cumulative cardiovascular risk in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We analyzed blood-based transcriptomics data from two independent cohorts: Seoul National University Bundang Hospital (SNUBH; N = 148, Korean) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI; N = 743, predominantly European ancestry). Framingham cardiovascular risk score (FRS)-associated co-expression network modules were identified, followed by pathway-based enrichment, hub gene-based participant stratification, and bidirectional cross-cohort discovery-replication analyses. RESULTS: Two co-expression modules were associated with FRS in SNUBH, and six in ADNI. Bidirectional analyses identified two preserved modules with consistent module-FRS associations across cohorts, enriched in pathways implicated in cellular responses to exposure, including RNA-protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and hematopoietic processes. Hub genes in the two modules stratified participants into molecularly distinct subgroups concordant with clinical FRS categories. DISCUSSION: FRS-associated molecular pathways were identified and warrant further investigation as potential targets for risk modification.

works.title: Mapping the evidence on the use of Alzheimer’s disease staging criteria (2011–2026): a scoping review to prioritise action for guidelines – protocol
works.abstract: ABSTRACT: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) staging has evolved rapidly with the introduction of biological definitions, expanded biomarker modalities and updated diagnostic frameworks. Multiple staging criteria are now used across research and clinical settings yet their real-world application remains unclear. Differences in healthcare infrastructure, biomarker availability and study purpose may influence how these criteria are implemented. This scoping review aims to systematically map how AD biological and clinical staging criteria have been used since 2011, characterise their application across study types and settings, and identify gaps that may inform future research and guideline development. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We will conduct a scoping review using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley and enhanced by Levac et al, and will report it according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guideline. We will search MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, PsycINFO and Scopus supplemented by forward-citation and backward-citation tracking using Web of Science. The review will begin in October 2026, with the baseline review complete by March 2027 and will be maintained as a living review. Two reviewers will independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts, extract data using a piloted charting form and resolve disagreements through discussion or a third reviewer. We will map study characteristics, staging criteria used, biomarker and clinical measures applied, outcomes assessed and how studies have examined progression or transitions between stages. We will also conduct a gap analysis to identify underexplored populations, outcomes and applications, with an expert panel convened by the Alzheimer’s Association reviewing and validating the identified gaps. Findings will be summarised descriptively using tables, figures and visualisations. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This review does not require ethics approval because it uses published data. We will disseminate the findings through peer-reviewed publication, conference presentations, webinars and plain-language summaries for people living with AD and their families. We will also share results with guideline developers and other stakeholders to support future evidence-based recommendations.

works.title: A single-center open-label, randomized, parallel-group controlled clinical trial on the long-term effect of the treatment with EGb 761 in blood markers of inflammation and neurodegeneration in patients with mild cognitive impairment: ACE-2020-EGb 761
works.abstract: BackgroundNeuroinflammation plays a central role in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and other dementias. EGb 761, a standardized Ginkgo biloba extract, has shown potential anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties.ObjectiveThis study evaluated the effects of EGb 761 on plasma proteins related to inflammation and neurodegeneration, cognitive performance, and core AD biomarkers in individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsWe conducted a 12-month randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial with a 12-month extension phase in 100 patients with MCI recruited at a single center. During the first 12 months, participants were randomly assigned to EGb 761 or no treatment. In the extension phase, all participants received EGb 761 for an additional 12 months. Plasma samples were collected at baseline and at 6-month intervals throughout both phases. Inflammatory and neurological proteomic profiles were assessed using the Olink Inflammation and Neurology panels. AD biomarkers including Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/40 ratio, GFAP, NfL, and pTau231 were measured in plasma. Clinical, neurological, and neuropsychological assessments were performed at each visit.ResultsEGb 761 was associated with nominally significant longitudinal decreases in 15 plasma proteins linked to innate immunity and axon guidance, replicated in the delayed-start group.ConclusionsEGb 761 exposure is associated with longitudinal modulation of serum markers associated with systemic inflammation and neurodegeneration in MCI. Larger placebo-controlled biomarker-driven trials are warranted to confirm whether this translates into clinically meaningful neuroprotection.Trial registration:Registro Español de estudios clínicos (REec) 2020-003776-41, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05594355, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05594355.

works.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Identifies Putative Pathogenic HNF1B Missense Variants Associated with HNF1B-MODY
works.abstract: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 5 (MODY5 or HNF1B-MODY) is a rare form of diabetes caused by variants in HNF1B. Patients with MODY5 exhibit high blood sugar levels and symptoms commonly associated with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with kidney and pancreatic issues. Nonetheless, diagnosis, treatment and management approaches depend on specific genotype-phenotype associations. Interpretation of HNF1B missense variants remains challenging because of conflicting classifications and limited clinical evidence. This study aimed to improve the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with conflicting evidence regarding pathogenicity and thereby advance the genetic and molecular understanding of HNF1B-MODY. An integrative computational approach combining artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and conventional bioinformatic tools, including Panther, SIFT, SNAP2, Meta-SNP, PhD-SNP, PolyPhen-2, and AlphaMissense, was used to identify deleterious missense variants in the HNF1B gene. The variants were further processed to determine their effects on protein conformation, stability, function, and conservation across species. Among 982 reported variants retrieved from the ClinVar database, 368 were classified as missense. Only 47 missense variants were labelled with conflicting classification and reported with clinical uncertainty. Consensus analysis by all tools identified five candidate variants (His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, Lys305Glu, and Val458Gly), representing 10.6% (5/47) as potentially pathogenic. AlphaMissense classified all five as likely pathogenic, with scores ranging from 0.8921 to 1.000. Secondary structure analysis indicates that the His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, and Lys305Glu variants are in the helical region, while the Val458Gly variant is located within the coil region. Interestingly, all five filtered variants are predicted by the I-Mutant and MuPro tools to reduce protein stability. The three-dimensional (3D) protein structures were constructed using the Deep Learning-Based Iterative Threading Assembly Refinement (D-I-TASSER) tool and visualised by UCSF Chimera. Structural modelling showed similarity between the mutant and wild-type models, with RMSD values ranging from 0.77 to 1.36 Å. The multiple sequence alignments show that amino acids at variant sites across all variants are highly conserved among species. These findings show that combining traditional bioinformatics with artificial intelligence and machine learning improves the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with clinical uncertainty. Integrating computational predictions with structural, evolutionary, and clinical data provides a framework for prioritising variants for further functional and clinical investigation.

works.title: Epistatic contributions to human traits via transcription factor mechanisms
works.abstract: Epistasis causes an individual's genetic background to modulate a DNA variant's effect on trait [1-6]. Epistatic interactions among different loci in human complex traits are expected to be widespread but have not been found [7]. This could be due to small interaction effect sizes, the statistical complexity of estimating interactions that is higher than marginal variant effects, and a substantial multiple testing burden in a genome-wide scan [8-11]. Targeting interacting variants that contribute to the same biological pathway could lighten this burden. Here we combined Targeted Machine Learning [12, 13] with experimentally verified differential binding variants across 9 nuclear hormone receptors (NHR) to identify 535 two-point DNA variant-variant and 185 three-point variant-variant-sex NHR interactions among 768 traits in the UK Biobank (UKB) at a false discovery rate per trait of less than 0.05. Significance testing combined k allele-specific components into a Hotelling's T 2 test of Average Interaction Effect estimates at pairs/triples of loci ( k ≤ 4 or k ≤ 8 for 2- or 3-point interactions, respectively). Nearly a third of 2-point interactions replicated, as they involved the same DNA-binding site and human trait but different trans-acting DNA variants. These epistatic mechanisms of altered transcription factor binding provide both plausible molecular mechanisms of action, and insight into sex-biased genetic risk, for diverse human traits and diseases.

works.title: Variants of Unknown Significance in Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young: High Rate of Conundrum Resolution via Variants of Unknown Significance Reanalysis
works.abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the era of next-generation sequencing, clinicians frequently encounter variants of unknown significance (VUS) in genetic testing. VUS may be reclassified over time as genetic knowledge grows. We know little about how best to approach VUS in the maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY). Therefore, our study aimed to determine the utility of reanalysis of previous VUS results in genetic confirmation of MODY. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review identified 85 subjects with a MODY clinical diagnosis. We reanalyzed genetic testing in 10 subjects with 14 unique VUS on MODY genes that was performed >3 years before the study. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical data was collected for those individuals. RESULTS: After reanalysis, 43% (6/14) of the gene variants were reclassified to a different category: 7% (1/14) were "likely pathogenic" and 36% (5/14) were "benign" or "likely benign." The reclassified pathogenic variant was in HNF1A and all reclassified benign variants were in HNF1A, HNF1B and PDX1. The median time between MODY testing and reclassification was 8 years (range: 4-10 years). CONCLUSION: In sum, iterative reanalyzing the genetic data from VUS found during MODY testing may provide high-yield diagnostic information. Further studies are warranted to identify the optimal time and frequency for such analyses.

works.title: The Reporting Quality of Machine Learning Studies on Pediatric Diabetes Mellitus: Systematic Review
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major health concern among children with the widespread adoption of advanced technologies. However, concerns are growing about the transparency, replicability, biasedness, and overall validity of artificial intelligence studies in medicine. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically review the reporting quality of machine learning (ML) studies of pediatric DM using the Minimum Information About Clinical Artificial Intelligence Modelling (MI-CLAIM) checklist, a general reporting guideline for medical artificial intelligence studies. METHODS: We searched the PubMed and Web of Science databases from 2016 to 2020. Studies were included if the use of ML was reported in children with DM aged 2 to 18 years, including studies on complications, screening studies, and in silico samples. In studies following the ML workflow of training, validation, and testing of results, reporting quality was assessed via MI-CLAIM by consensus judgments of independent reviewer pairs. Positive answers to the 17 binary items regarding sufficient reporting were qualitatively summarized and counted as a proxy measure of reporting quality. The synthesis of results included testing the association of reporting quality with publication and data type, participants (human or in silico), research goals, level of code sharing, and the scientific field of publication (medical or engineering), as well as with expert judgments of clinical impact and reproducibility. RESULTS: After screening 1043 records, 28 studies were included. The sample size of the training cohort ranged from 5 to 561. Six studies featured only in silico patients. The reporting quality was low, with great variation among the 21 studies assessed using MI-CLAIM. The number of items with sufficient reporting ranged from 4 to 12 (mean 7.43, SD 2.62). The items on research questions and data characterization were reported adequately most often, whereas items on patient characteristics and model examination were reported adequately least often. The representativeness of the training and test cohorts to real-world settings and the adequacy of model performance evaluation were the most difficult to judge. Reporting quality improved over time (r=0.50; P=.02); it was higher than average in prognostic biomarker and risk factor studies (P=.04) and lower in noninvasive hypoglycemia detection studies (P=.006), higher in studies published in medical versus engineering journals (P=.004), and higher in studies sharing any code of the ML pipeline versus not sharing (P=.003). The association between expert judgments and MI-CLAIM ratings was not significant. CONCLUSIONS: The reporting quality of ML studies in the pediatric population with DM was generally low. Important details for clinicians, such as patient characteristics; comparison with the state-of-the-art solution; and model examination for valid, unbiased, and robust results, were often the weak points of reporting. To assess their clinical utility, the reporting standards of ML studies must evolve, and algorithms for this challenging population must become more transparent and replicable.

works.title: Insights from basic adjunctive examinations of GCK‐MODY , HNF1A‐MODY , and type 2 diabetes: A systemic review and meta‐analysis
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glucokinase maturity-onset diabetes of the young (GCK-MODY) is difficult to distinguish from other diabetic forms. This article aims to characterize the differences in results from routine examinations between GCK-MODY and hepatocyte nuclear factor 1-α (HNF1A)-MODY or type 2 diabetes (T2D) patients in different periods of diabetes. METHODS: Ovid Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up until October 9, 2022 for articles containing baseline characteristics of GCK-MODY, HNF1A-MOFY, and T2D, excluding pregnant women. The pooled standardized mean differences were derived using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Compared to HNF1A-MODY, GCK-MODY patients had lower indicators of glucose metabolism. Total triglycerides (TG) (-0.93 [-1.66, -0.21] mmol/l) were consistently lower in GCK-MODY patients in the all-family-members subgroup analysis. Compared to T2D, GCK-MODY patients were younger at diagnosis and had lower body mass index (BMI), lower high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) (-0.60 [-0.75, -0.44] mg/l), lower fasting C-peptide (FCP), and lower 2-hour postprandial glucose (2-h PG). Indicators of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and fasting blood glucose (FPG) were consistently lower in subgroup studies with all family members of GCK-MODY patients as well. CONCLUSIONS: Lower HbA1c, FPG, 2-h PG, and change in 2-h PG may help to diagnose GCK-MODY differentially from HNF1A-MODY at an early stage, and lower TG may strengthen such a diagnosis in the follow-up stages. Younger age combined with lower BMI, FCP, hsCRP, and 2-h PG may be useful to distinguish GCK-MODY from MODY-like T2D, whereas results of glucose metabolism indicators such as HbA1c and FPG may not help physicians until after a long follow-up period.

works.title: The Genetics of Type 2 Diabetes in Youth: Where We Are and the Road Ahead

works.title: Meta-analysis of HNF1A-MODY3 variants among human population
works.abstract: BackgroundPreviously, numerous case-control studies have highlighted variants responsible for Maturity onset diabetes of young (MODY). However, these studies have been conducted among diverse populations and hence yielded contradictory results. We, therefore, performed a meta-analysis to precisely find the association of SNPs with the disease for the HNF1A gene.ObjectiveMeta-analysis of clinically defined studies deciphering mutations in the HNF1A gene responsible for the development of MODY3 was conducted among various populations to determine associations using statistical approaches. MethodsThe curation of 505 research articles published between the years 2000-2021 was carried out. Visualization of data-related protocols and statistical-analysis were conducted, which led to the identification of highly prevalent mutations among different populations (majorly Europe). Further comparison between the frequencies of the control (healthy population) and test (diseased population) dataset generated through curation was performed.ResultsWe identified nine MODY3 mutations (rs587776825, rs1169288, rs1800574, rs2464196, rs137853244, rs137853238, rs587780357, rs137853240 and rs137853243) at the genome-wide significance level (p<5.0×10–8). The present study confirmed that the data does not follow a normal distribution. Further, the data was confirmed to be a more homogenous type with frequencies having a significant association with the disease.Conclusion﻿This meta-analysis found significant associations of mutations in HNF1A with MODY3, consistent with previous studies. Our findings should help elucidate the mutations in a compiled form responsible for causing MODY3.

works.title: Euclid preparation: CXII. Baryon acoustic oscillations extraction techniques: comparison and optimisation
works.abstract: We present the first end-to-end validation of the Euclid baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analysis pipeline, encompassing density-field reconstruction, two-point correlation function measurement, and cosmological parameter inference. Using eight Euclid -like mock catalogues extracted from each of the four snapshots of the Flagship 1 (FS1) simulation, which is designed to replicate the statistical properties of the first Euclid data release (DR1), we assessed the performance of the two standard BAO reconstruction methods based on the Zeldovich approximation, R EC S YM and R EC I SO, in four redshift snapshots (0.9 ≤ z ≤ 1.8). The pipeline introduces several methodological advances: an emulator-based model evaluator (Bora.jl) combined with a Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampler (NUTS), achieving a speed-up of more than 500 times relative to standard Monte Carlo Markov chains, and a semi-analytical covariance estimator (BeXiCov+WinCov) that enables robust error estimates with only eight mock realisations and remains stable under variations in the fiducial cosmology. Together, these components ensure computational efficiency while significantly reducing the risk of underestimating the parameter uncertainties. The two reconstruction schemes yield unbiased BAO measurements for all redshifts and user-defined choices, including the smoothing scale and fiducial cosmology. In each snapshot, reconstruction enhances the figure of merit for {Ω m, H 0 r s } by a factor of ∼3, which is equivalent to tripling the effective survey volume. When we combined the four redshift bins, the improvement remained substantial, with BAO-only constraints reaching ∼10% precision on Ω m and ∼3% on H 0 r s. The results from R EC S YM and R EC I SO are consistent within the uncertainties, but we recommend R EC S YM during testing because its sensitivity to covariance variations is lower. These findings establish the accuracy, robustness, and scalability of the Euclid BAO pipeline for DR1 and provide a solid foundation for future cosmological analyses.

works.title: Novel constraints on the particle nature of dark matter from stellar streams
works.venue: Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
works.abstract: Tidal streams are highly sensitive to perturbations from passing dark matter (DM) subhalos and thus provide a means of measuring their abundance. In a recent paper, we analyzed the distribution of stars along the GD-1 stream with a combination of data from the Gaia satellite and the Pan-STARRS survey, and we demonstrated that the population of DM subhalos predicted by the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm are necessary and sufficient to explain the perturbations observed in the linear density of stars. In this paper, we use the measurements of the subhalo mass function (SHMF) from the GD-1 data combined with a similar analysis of the Pal 5 stream to provide novel constraints on alternative DM scenarios that predict a suppression of the SHMF on scales smaller than the mass of dwarf galaxies, marginalizing over uncertainties in the slope and normalization of the unsuppressed SHMF and the susceptibility of DM subhalos in the inner Milky Way to tidal disruption. In particular, we derive a 95% lower limit on the mass of warm dark matter (WDM) thermal relics m WDM > 3.6 keV from streams alone that strengthens to m WDM > 6.2 keV when adding dwarf satellite counts. Similarly, we constrain the axion mass in ultra-light ("fuzzy") dark matter (FDM) models to be m FDM > 1.4 × 10 -21 eV from streams alone or m FDM > 2.2 × 10 -21 eV when adding dwarf satellite counts. Because we make use of simple approximate forms of the streams' SHMF measurement, our analysis is easy to replicate with other alternative DM models that lead to a suppression of the SHMF.

works.title: A divergence-free parametrization for dynamical dark energy
works.venue: Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
works.abstract: We introduce a new parametrization for the dark energy, led by the same idea to the linear expansion of the equation of state in scale factor a and in redshift z , which diverges neither in the past nor future and contains the same number of degrees of freedom with the former two. We present constraints of the cosmological parameters using the most updated baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements along with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data and a recent reanalysis of Type Ia supernova (SN) data. This new parametrization allowed us to carry out successive observational analyses by decreasing its degrees of freedom systematically until ending up with a dynamical dark energy model that has the same number of parameters with ΛCDM . We found that the dark energy source with a dynamical equation of state parameter equal −2/3 at the early universe and −1 today fits the data slightly better than Λ.

works.title: The association between boredom and creativity in educational contexts: A scoping review on research approaches and empirical findings
works.abstract: Assumptions around the association between boredom and creativity are contentious. Although studies suggest positive effects of boredom, it is also considered a negative predictor of creativity. Researchers also assume that creativity reduces boredom, but boredom can also occur during creative tasks. In this review, we identify and systematise the empirical evidence available to date on the association between creativity and boredom in educational contexts. The string‐guided electronic search yielded 2849 publications. Nineteen publications based on 27 empirical studies met the inclusion criteria. Two reviewers extracted definitions, theories, methods, operationalisations, measurement instruments, and outcomes from the studies using a coding scheme. We identified a range of different theoretical and methodological approaches. The largest cache of empirical evidence was obtained from experimental and quasi‐experimental studies (five positive associations, four negative, two contradictory, and three insignificant results). Correlation studies identified three negative, one contradictory, and seven insignificant correlations between boredom and creativity. In addition, two studies with exploratory, statistically not relevant results contributed to the body of research. The results from the identified and evaluated studies argue both for and against the sensitivity of creative processes in relation to boredom—but a clear causal, positive or negative effect of boredom on creativity is not currently supported by the empirical evidence available. Previous research has also not yet demonstrated an apparent effect of creative states or traits on academic boredom. Future research should aim to explore under what circumstances different relationships between boredom and creativity can be observed and reliably replicated.
